clue.text: Behind everybody, in spite of any indications to the contrary

definitions.text: in spite of any indications to the contrary

parts.note: behind in time or order means after
everybody is all

explanation.surface: Someone trails the whole field yet insists the signs pointed otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to concede that something holds despite earlier suggestions, as in 'he came after all'.

clue.text: Land on fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to come down and settle, as a bird or passenger does

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a plane or region in flames; the two parts are separate meanings, a verb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to descend and settle, and the adjective means burning or lit up.

clue.text: Dreamt about problem with exercise machine

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and moved into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
an ill is a trouble or problem

explanation.surface: Someone had a nightmare about a fault on their gym equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a gym device with a moving belt for walking or running on the spot.

clue.text: Proportion kept by corporation

indicators.note: kept by means held inside the following word, so the answer sits within its letters

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word, after its first four

explanation.surface: A share or quota retained by a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the proportion of one quantity to another.

clue.text: A lot enjoy article on Victorian novelist

parts.note: to enjoy is to like
the definite article
Charles Dickens, the Victorian author

explanation.surface: A reader is a big fan of a piece about a nineteenth-century writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an intensifier meaning very much or a great deal, as in 'it hurt like the dickens'.

clue.text: Animal in mountain pasture, a cat with no tail

indicators.note: having no tail means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an alp is high grazing land on a mountainside
taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A tailless cat wanders through a high meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American domesticated animal related to the llama, kept for its wool.

clue.text: Zest shown by former PM supporting the French on Monday

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means holding up from below, so the prime minister goes second, under the rest

parts.note: le is a French word for 'the'
the standard abbreviation for Monday
Sir Robert Peel was a British prime minister in the 1830s and 1840s

explanation.surface: An ex-premier shows enthusiasm while backing the French at the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supporting' puts the prime minister underneath, so he comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the grated outer rind of a citrus fruit, here the lemon's.

clue.text: Nazi shot bearing down on old Allied landing site

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A German soldier is fired upon as he advances on an old wartime beachhead.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the anagram sits above, or bearing down on, the abbreviation for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Anzio in Italy was where Allied troops made an amphibious landing in January 1944.

clue.text: Deserter, a Pole, put away

parts.note: taken as written
a post is an upright pole
to put food away is to eat it

explanation.surface: A Polish runaway has been locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Pole look like a Polish person; it is just a stake, and 'put away' means eaten, not jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a religion or cause, a deserter of their faith.

clue.text: Order, on board — hold and slacken three sheets in the wind

indicators.note: an idiom for being very drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A sailing instruction about gripping and easing ropes, given by a sailor who is thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheets' are also ropes on a ship, which helps the nautical disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the command calling the whole crew up on deck, an order given aboard ship.

clue.text: It holds writer back being cack-handed

indicators.note: holds means the outer word wraps around something placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word for the writer runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Something keeps an author from progressing because it is so clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cack-handed is British slang for clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone clumsy or lacking skill.

clue.text: Musical instrument broken by priest in US city

indicators.note: broken by means the first word is split open with something put into the gap

parts.note: a kazoo is a small humming instrument
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A cleric smashes a musical instrument somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalamazoo is a city in Michigan in the United States.

clue.text: Retreat from mostly horrific conflict, finally

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word is used, dropping its final letter

parts.note: hideous means horrific; trimmed of its last letter

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of conflict

explanation.surface: Soldiers withdraw from a dreadful war at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like a verb about withdrawing from battle; it is a noun, a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a secluded place to hide, a refuge or retreat.

clue.text: Worker abroad getting financial support

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
abroad can mean out and about, outside

explanation.surface: An employee overseas receives a subsidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A handout is money or goods given as aid, a form of financial assistance.

clue.text: Mere hobby bringing one a return on investment

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than
a hobby is an interest pursued for pleasure

explanation.surface: A modest pastime turns out to earn someone some money.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple interest is the return calculated only on the original sum invested, not on accrued interest.

clue.text: Pieman Tom transformed Christmas show

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker called Tom is magically changed into a festive entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime is a British family stage show put on at Christmas, full of slapstick and transformation scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomimes are the traditional festive-season theatre productions in Britain.

clue.text: Friedman, say, comes in to broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous name arrives at the studio to go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Milton Friedman as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Friedman was a Nobel-winning American economist, so he is an instance of the profession.

clue.text: Murderer, casing outhouse, seized an advantage

indicators.note: casing means encasing or enclosing, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
a shed is an outhouse

explanation.surface: A killer scouts out a garden building, then grabs his chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casing' looks like a burglar's word for reconnoitring; it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash in on something is to exploit or profit from an opportunity.

clue.text: Fish in a canal — smolt, possibly, around end of August

indicators.note: possibly hints at one of several arrangements, and around says the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of August

explanation.surface: A young salmon is seen in a canal in late summer.
explanation.walkthrough: A smolt is a young salmon, so the clue is a nice nudge; 'in' belongs with the letters to shuffle, not with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic salmon is a species of fish found in North Atlantic rivers and seas.

clue.text: Cut off by northern river

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A northern waterway has left a place isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and western England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is a major British river, rising in Wales and reaching the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Fish, shad, missing head and tail

indicators.note: missing its head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written, before beheading
the dock is the solid fleshy part of an animal's tail

explanation.surface: A shad is served without its head and tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head and tail' looks like one instruction; only the head goes, and 'tail' supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Duke left out pottery

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of place and rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Duke
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aristocrat omitted the china.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of that name.

clue.text: French resort, on western end of estuary, is very good

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
taken as written

indicators.note: in an across entry the west is the left, so this means the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of estuary

explanation.surface: A Riviera town at the mouth of a river is a great place.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is informal British praise meaning well done, an idiom for very good.

clue.text: Beast of burden arrived, then left

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, to arrive
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A pack animal turned up and then departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels are used to carry loads across deserts, a classic pack animal.

clue.text: Daughter's marriage in amorous play

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a marriage is an alliance between families

explanation.surface: A girl's wedding turns into a flirtation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance means casual romantic or flirtatious behaviour, amorous play.

clue.text: Principal eastern US state

parts.note: principal means main or chief
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A description of an important state on America's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the northeasternmost state of the United States.

clue.text: One regarded as mad in northern state

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
to state is to utter or say

explanation.surface: Someone thought crazy lives in the north of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a region; it is a verb, to say. Nutter is British slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutter is informal British slang for an eccentric or crazy person.

clue.text: Knee lost? Could be in this set of bones

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else once reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A missing kneecap might be found within someone's frame of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the full framework of bones supporting a body.
